sentences.english: My father may fix the broken door himself, because he has already fixed many things in the house before.
sentences.grammar_focus: قَدْ + present for "may" (قَدْ يُصْلِحُ) against قَدْ + past for "has (already)" (قَدْ أَصْلَحَ), a passive participle as a definite adjective (البابَ المَكْسورَ), بِنَفْسِهِ for "himself", and the diptote أَشْياء with a feminine singular adjective (أَشْياءَ كَثيرَةً)
sentences.model_answer: قَدْ يُصْلِحُ أَبي البابَ المَكْسورَ بِنَفْسِهِ، لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ أَصْلَحَ أَشْياءَ كَثيرَةً في البَيْتِ مِنْ قَبْلُ.

mistakes.rule: An adjective of a definite noun takes ال: المكسور

باب is masculine: البابَ المكسورَ.
"Himself": بنفسِه.
البابَ المكسورَ نفسَه is "the broken door itself". "By himself": بنفسِه.
This door in particular: البابَ المكسورَ.

sentences.english: My sister surprised me with a gift she had made with her own hands, and it was the most beautiful surprise this year.
sentences.grammar_focus: فاجَأَ with an object pronoun and بِـ (فاجَأَتْني أُخْتي بِهَدِيَّةٍ), a relative clause on an indefinite noun with no التي and a returning pronoun (هَدِيَّةٍ صَنَعَتْها), the genitive dual after بِـ (بِيَدَيْها), and the superlative + indefinite singular (أَجْمَلَ مُفاجَأَةٍ) after a feminine كانت
sentences.model_answer: فاجَأَتْني أُخْتي بِهَدِيَّةٍ صَنَعَتْها بِيَدَيْها، وَكانَتْ أَجْمَلَ مُفاجَأَةٍ هٰذا العامَ.
reference_translations: فاجأتني أختي بهدية صنعتها بيديها وكانت أجمل مفاجأة هذا العام

mistakes.note: With أختي as subject the verb takes تْ: فاجأتْني أختي.
After a fatha with a sukun on it, the hamza sits on alif: فاجَأَتْني.

mistakes.rule: "Surprised me": فاجأتني (the pronoun joins the verb)

mistakes.rule: After an indefinite noun, no التي: بهدية صنعتها
mistakes.note: A relative clause after an indefinite noun has no التي/الذي: بهديّةٍ صنعتْها.

mistakes.rule: After بـ the dual is genitive: بيديها
mistakes.note: بـ makes the dual genitive: بيدَيْها (not بيداها).

هديّة is feminine, so the returning pronoun is ـها: صنعتْها.

mistakes.rule: The first noun of an idafa takes no ال
mistakes.note: "Washing the clothes": غسلِ الملابسِ, with ال only on الملابس.

mistakes.rule: عدم heads an idafa: عدم غسل
mistakes.note: عدم is the first noun of the idafa, so it takes no ال: عدمِ غسلِ الملابس.
لم + jussive: لم أغسلْ, not لم غسلتُ.

mistakes.rule: A length of time is accusative: أسبوعا كاملا
mistakes.note: "For a whole week": أسبوعًا كاملًا (or لمدة أسبوعٍ كاملٍ).

mistakes.rule: A length of time is accusative: أسبوعا كاملا
mistakes.note: "For a whole week": أسبوعًا كاملًا (or لمدة أسبوعٍ كاملٍ).

mistakes.rule: The predicate of أصبح is accusative and feminine: وسخة
mistakes.note: أصبحت كلّها وسخةً: accusative after أصبح, feminine for things.
ملابس are things, so "all of them" is كلّها.

mistakes.rule: Things take a feminine singular verb: أصبحت
mistakes.note: ملابس are things: أصبحتْ, not أصبحوا.
وسخين is for people. Things: وسخةً.

mistakes.rule: Things take a feminine verb: أصبحت
mistakes.note: Before كلّها (for الملابس) the verb is feminine: أصبحتْ.
